summary: Best config (0.980742 vs 0.997359 baseline, -0.0166) stacks six changes on the shipped train.py: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^19->2^18 (grad_accum 2->1, ~2x optimizer steps, -0.0079); short sliding window 1024->512 with WINDOW_PATTERN 'SSL' (3 of 8 layers full-context, -0.0025); value embeddings on ALL layers instead of every other (-0.0016); MLP expansion 4x->6x with MATRIX_LR retuned 0.04->0.03 (-0.0017); attention softmax_scale 1/sqrt(128)->0.12, the right temperature once q/k are rms-normed (-0.0004); EMBEDDING_LR 0.6->0.32 (-0.0011). The clear theme: FLOPs are precious in 5 minutes, so buy capacity where it is cheap (embedding lookups, FFN width) and cut it where it is not (attention window). What did not work: bigger/deeper models at wider dim, finer heads (head_dim 64 is worse in both quality and MFU), U-net skip connections, token smear, gated relu^2 MLP at matched cost, MLP 3x or 8x, and compiler-side throughput tuning (coordinate_descent_tuning was a net loss and nearly blew the 600s timeout). Next I would push EMBEDDING_LR lower still (0.32 was the last run and the trend was still improving), re-probe head_dim 256 together with a matched softmax_scale ~0.06 (the 64->128 step was worth 0.0073 at equal tokens, so fatter heads may keep paying), and split the LR of the value-embedding tables from wte now that there are 8 of them.
